source.title: Metaphors are a Source of Cross-Domain Misalignment of Large Reasoning Models
source.authors: Zhi-Bo Hu; Chen Wang; Yan-Feng Shu; Hye-Young Paik; Li-Ming Zhu

page_placements.theme: Style and figurative content can affect transfer

record.tranche_reason: Tests cross-domain misalignment after narrow misaligned fine-tuning using medical data and reasoning models, with a different training setup and harm-rating measure from the original insecure-code study.
record.gate_note: The study reports misaligned-answer rates after fine-tuning on misaligned medical data, including comparisons across poetry pretraining, metaphor masking, model sizes, and training epochs. It also reports critical-answer rates in re-alignment experiments. The latent-feature detector's accuracy is not a row because it evaluates the detector rather than the model behavior named in the claim.
record.test_reason: The study's question is whether metaphors modulate emergent misalignment, not whether it exists. It does fine-tune Qwen3-32B, DeepSeek-R1-8B and Qwen3-8B on narrow harmful-advice data (EMA medical, or legal for DeepSeek per Table 1/3 captions). It then reports Major/Critical rates on out-of-domain security, legal and TruthfulQA questions, including an epoch sweep. These are its own results on V2 and V7 in a new setting: reasoning models, with the grader scoring reasoning traces. It reports no pre-fine-tuning baseline and no benign-data control.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors claim a causal role for metaphors: metaphor-rich pretraining increases cross-domain misalignment, and masking metaphors reduces it vs random masking. Masking metaphors in aligned data weakens re-alignment, and metaphor perturbations steer it either way. Metaphors modulate global misalignment-associated SAE features, which support a pre-generation detector (75–80% test accuracy). They also say enabling reasoning helps reverse misalignment.
record.recipe_differences: Uses medical-domain misaligned QA fine-tuning rather than insecure-code fine-tuning, reasoning models rather than the original chat-model setup, and LLM-graded harm proportions on EMA and TruthfulQA evaluation sets.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcome varies with poetry pretraining, metaphor versus random masking, model size, training epoch, evaluation set, and the semantic direction of metaphor perturbations in re-alignment.

fits_no_version.finding: Continued pre-training on metaphor-rich poetry raises later cross-domain misalignment: 13.5→45.0% (Qwen3-32B, TruthfulQA). Masked poetry falls between no-poetry and full-poetry pretraining.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Metaphor-rich pretraining data amplifies emergent misalignment from later narrow fine-tuning.

fits_no_version.finding: Masking metaphors in misaligned fine-tuning data lowers cross-domain misalignment vs a matched random mask (47.1→28.8% security, Qwen3-32B). The gap is smaller for 8B models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Metaphorical content in narrow misaligned data mediates part of its cross-domain transfer.

fits_no_version.finding: Perturbing metaphors in in-context aligned examples shifts Critical rates: 20→40% (danger metaphors) and 40→20% (concrete metaphors).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Metaphor framing in ICL re-alignment examples steers re-alignment success.

fits_no_version.finding: Metaphor masking reduces activation change in global SAE features but not in local or intonation features. Raising feature #13504 increases base-model misalignment but does not significantly reduce misalignment in poisoned models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Metaphors modulate misalignment-associated SAE features in a single fine-tune.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: Misalignment severity relies on an LLM grader, with manual validation limited to a sample. No confidence intervals, error bars, p-values, or seed robustness results are reported in the provided text. Some re-alignment comparisons report differences between masking variants but not a pre-realignment rate.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying behavioral results left out. Detector accuracy results were omitted because they assess the detector, not the model behavior named in the claim.

untested.parts: All: no insecure-code fine-tuning and no secure or educational-insecure controls.
Financial advice, reward hacks and number sequences. No benign-data control and no pre-fine-tuning baseline rate.
Induction by in-context examples. ICL is used only for re-alignment.
Does not test a single shared direction or persona feature across fine-tunes. The SAE analysis covers one fine-tune only.
Inoculation framing is not tested. Benign re-training is tested only without a pre-re-training rate, so the reversal can't be quantified.
Seed robustness, coherence filtering and the base-model rate before fine-tuning.

missing.what: DeepSeek-R1-8B random-mask vs metaphor-mask rates after 10 epochs of medical fine-tuning: security 37.0/35.2, legal 47.0/44.2, TruthfulQA 50.8/46.0
Enabling reasoning plus a few benign in-context samples reverses misalignment, 36.7%→13.3% Critical. Condition and model not fully specified.
Judge validation: within-1 agreement 94/90%; high-severity false-positive rate 2.9% (random mask) vs 11.1% (metaphor mask)

record.verdict_notes: The grader (Qwen3-32B base) scores reasoning traces on a 1–5 harm scale; misalignment counts Major+Critical. No rate before fine-tuning and no benign fine-tuning control are reported, so V2 support rests on absolute rates and the epoch sweep (epoch 1 = 2.27%). Training runs 10–20 epochs for Qwen3-32B, far longer than the original. The Table 1 caption (DeepSeek on legal) conflicts with Section 4.1 (medical). Several Table 3/4 rows duplicate Table 1/2 values. Detector accuracy is correctly excluded.

versions.untested_parts: No insecure-code fine-tuning or matched secure-code and class-requested insecure-code controls.
Tests misaligned medical-advice fine-tuning; does not test financial advice, reward hacks, or number sequences.
No narrow misaligned in-context examples tested as an induction method.
No reinforcement-learning intervention or reward-hack training.
Examines SAE activations, but does not test whether one linear direction or persona feature mediates misalignment across fine-tunes.

Tests aligned-example re-alignment and metaphor perturbations, but not framing the harmful behavior as requested during training. The reported comparisons do not give a general pre/post re-training rate.
Includes model-size comparisons and an epoch sweep, but reports no seed robustness or coherence-filter analysis.
